description: State management controls how data flows and updates in a React Native application.

useState.description: Local state hook for functional components. Returns a stateful value and a function to update it.

useReducer.description: Alternative to useState for complex state logic involving multiple sub-values or when the next state depends on the previous one.

useContext.description: Accepts a context object and returns the current context value for that context. Used for global state.

Props Drilling.description: Passing data from parent to child through multiple layers of components.
Props Drilling.note: Avoid excessive props drilling; use Context or State Libraries instead.

Context API.description: Built-in React API to share values like themes or auth status between components without explicitly passing a prop.

Redux / Zustand.description: External libraries for managing global state in larger applications.
Redux / Zustand.note: Useful when state logic becomes too complex for Context API.

Immutability.description: State should never be modified directly. Always use the setter function provided by the hook.

Asynchronous Updates.description: State updates may not happen immediately. React batches updates for performance.

Unidirectional Data Flow.description: Data flows down from parent to child via props.

bestPractices: Keep state as local as possible. Lift state up only when necessary.
Use multiple useState hooks for independent variables instead of one large object.
Use Context for truly global data (Auth, Theme, Language).
Avoid storing derived state. Calculate it on the fly or use useMemo.
